observed.pre_delta_gap: The current supervisor derived provider admission before explicit secret-file loading and provider network, but already-inherited provider credential environment variables were not removed before spawning child processes. Child environment inheritance therefore left a residual secret-exposure path even while provider execution was quarantined.

hypothesis: Removing only credential variable names belonging to non-admitted external LLM providers before every child spawn closes inherited-environment exposure without weakening the canonical typed admission authority or expanding blocked secret values.
counterhypothesis: Downstream provider gates are sufficient because children cannot execute unadmitted provider requests. Rejected as a complete secret-boundary argument: downstream network denial does not prevent an unrelated child process from inheriting credential material it has no need or authority to possess.

properties: fails closed on nonzero/malformed/not-admitted provider result
unsets Groq/Mistral/NVIDIA/OpenRouter credential variables by name
uses compgen -v only to enumerate suffixed variable names
does not expand blocked credential values to decide removal
does not add a second provider authority or secret store

coverage: all four current external LLM providers have negative-admission clearing branches
fixed and suffixed credential variable families are present
fence ordering precedes every child-start function in the supervisor loop
